Top research papers on multi-agent orchestration, grouped by surveys, foundational frameworks, and benchmark/failure evaluations:

### 1. Surveys and Taxonomies
- [Large language model based multi-agents: A survey of progress and challenges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01680) (Guo et al., 2024, arXiv:2402.01680): Classifies multi-agent architectures, agent profiling, coordination mechanisms, and communication paradigms.
- [Multi-agent collaboration mechanisms: A survey of LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06322) (Tran et al., 2025, arXiv:2501.06322): Reviews coordination frameworks, collaborative mechanisms, and orchestration dynamics across LLM systems.
- [A survey on LLM-based multi-agent systems: workflow, infrastructure, and challenges](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44336-024-00009-2) (Li et al., 2024, *Vicinagearth*, Springer): Focuses on orchestration workflows, information exchange, infrastructure models, and action coordination.
- [Beyond self-talk: A communication-centric survey of LLM-based multi-agent systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14321) (Yan et al., 2025, arXiv:2502.14321): Evaluates multi-agent topologies, message-passing structures, protocol designs, and task execution workflows.
- [A survey of multi-AI agent collaboration: Theories, technologies and applications](https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3745238.3745531) (Zhang et al., 2025, ACM): Covers theoretical coordination foundations, multimodal integration, and multi-agent task execution.

### 2. Foundational Orchestration Frameworks
- [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) (Wu et al., 2023, arXiv:2308.08155): Introduces conversable agent architecture with dynamic routing, group chat orchestration, and code/natural-language-driven control topologies across LLMs, tools, and humans.
- [ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924) (Qian et al., 2023/2024, ACL 2024 / arXiv:2307.07924): Formulates a communicative phase-gated execution graph (design, coding, testing) using multi-agent role-playing dialogues.

### 3. Benchmarks, Coordination Overhead, and Failure Attribution
- [Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11600) (Liao et al., 2026, arXiv:2610.11600): Evaluates failure cascades on the Who&When benchmark using the EMFA framework with candidate screening and counterfactual verification (+3.45% and +4.40% recovery attribution).
- [EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01360) (Hou et al., 2026, EMNLP 2026 / arXiv:2609.01360): Evaluates multi-error dependencies and compound execution failures across multi-agent graphs.
- [DCFA: Dual-view Causal-inspired Attribution for Failure Reasoning in LLM-based Multi-agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04749) (Wang et al., 2026, arXiv:2609.04749): Evaluates coordination overhead and causal attribution, disentangling task-flow dependencies from inter-agent communications.
- [From Investigation Failures to Reliable SOC Agents: Understanding and Improving LLM-Based Alert Triage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10608) (Tsegai et al., 2026, arXiv:2610.10608): Benchmarks complex orchestration on ALERT-BENCH (1,247 telemetry alerts), analyzing coordination failures and evidence omission in multi-agent loops.
- [Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10628) (Tang et al., 2026, ASE@POVC 2026 / arXiv:2610.10628): Evaluates structured iterative consensus mechanisms versus basic multi-agent prompting on the E2E Requirements Engineering Benchmark.

### Missing and Uncertain Information
- Framework coverage is incomplete: other standard graph-centric multi-agent architectures (such as MetaGPT, LangGraph, or CAMEL) were not retrieved due to search limit constraints.
- Full PDF metrics and exact taxonomy sub-branches for Springer and ACM survey papers, as well as baseline metric tables for EDGE and DCFA, were not extracted because agents only accessed abstract pages and metadata. Platforms like OpenReview, Semantic Scholar, and Papers with Code were not queried.

- Status: COMPLETED (Worker: worker_benchmarks_and_evaluation_1b1f1981, Tab: tab_benchmarks_and_evaluation_a58f56)
- Findings: ### Findings
- [Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11600) | **Authors:** Jiaqi Liao, Yuanzhao Zhai, Huanxi Liu, Xu Zhang, Zheming Zhuang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Huaimin Wang | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Who&When benchmark | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2610.11600 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Step-level attribution accuracy, agent-level attribution accuracy | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Addresses failure cascading across multi-agent interactions and persistent loops where downstream symptoms mask decisive root-cause steps. Proposes EMFA (Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution) using candidate screening and counterfactual verification, outperforming prior baselines by 3.45% and 4.40% on Who&When Hand-Crafted and Algorithm-Generated subsets. | **Evidence:** Page abstract explicitly defines decisive error attribution as identifying the agent-step pair whose correction recovers execution, and reports evaluation on the Who&When benchmark. | **Relevance:** Directly evaluates multi-agent failure propagation, root-cause attribution, and error-recovery evaluation across interacting agents.

- [EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01360) | **Authors:** Jun Hou, Priya Pitre, Yi Fang, Xuan Wang | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Who&When benchmark suite (multi-error failure attribution) | **Venue:** EMNLP 2026 (`arXiv:2609.01360 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Multi-error attribution precision/recall, error dependency identification accuracy | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Multi-agent system executions often fail due to compounded, interdependent errors across multiple agents rather than single isolated mistakes. Graph-guided modeling disentangles cascading agent failures from concurrent execution bugs. | **Evidence:** ArXiv search record indicates acceptance at EMNLP 2026 and abstract focuses on multi-error attribution in LLM agent systems. | **Relevance:** Targets empirical failure-mode decomposition and multi-agent coordination breakdowns in complex execution graphs.

- [DCFA: Dual-view Causal-inspired Attribution for Failure Reasoning in LLM-based Multi-agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04749) | **Authors:** Zehao Wang, Lanjun Wang, Shilong Jin, Junjie Chen, Yanghua Xiao | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Multi-agent failure reasoning benchmarks (including Who&When evaluation suite) | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2609.04749 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Causal attribution accuracy, agent-level fault identification | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Multi-agent collaboration increases overhead in causal tracing; dual-view causal reasoning separates task-flow dependencies from inter-agent communication dynamics to diagnose orchestration breakdowns. | **Evidence:** ArXiv listing confirms methodology focused on failure reasoning and causal attribution in LLM multi-agent systems. | **Relevance:** Establishes evaluation methodology for failure attribution in orchestrated LLM agent environments.

- [From Investigation Failures to Reliable SOC Agents: Understanding and Improving LLM-Based Alert Triage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10608) | **Authors:** Saimon Amanuel Tsegai, Alex Kantchelian, Danfeng Yao, Peng Gao | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** ALERT-BENCH | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2610.10608 [cs.CR, cs.AI, cs.MA]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Multi-stage attack detection rate, evidence retrieval fidelity across 1,247 telemetry alerts, triage error rate | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Evaluates iterative retrieval, self-review, and multi-agent verification loops in enterprise security operations; reveals that every tested orchestration setup suffered investigation failures across complex multi-stage attack scenarios due to coordination degradation and evidence omission. | **Evidence:** Page abstract states: "ALERT-BENCH, an interactive benchmark that replays enterprise telemetry through a live SIEM... Across 1,247 alerts from a multi-stage attack scenario, every approach missed critical attack steps". | **Relevance:** Empirical benchmark explicitly measuring multi-agent triage workflows, coordination overhead, and systemic failure modes in specialized environments.

- [Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10628) | **Authors:** Yongjian Tang, Linhan Li, Thomas Runkler | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** E2E Requirements Engineering Benchmark (Zenodo record `22815961`) | **Venue:** ASE@POVC 2026 (`arXiv:2610.10628 [cs.SE, cs.AI]`, DOI: 10.1145/3843779.3844634) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Requirement refinement completeness, inter-agent consensus score, specification generation fidelity | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Basic agent collaboration under-utilizes multi-agent potential due to lack of self-refining consensus mechanisms; structured iterative multi-agent coordination improves software specification accuracy over rudimentary prompting. | **Evidence:** ArXiv listing details benchmark publication on Zenodo and acceptance to the ASE@POVC track. | **Relevance:** Measures orchestration efficiency and consensus trade-offs in end-to-end software engineering pipelines.

### Coverage
- **Platforms Searched:** arXiv (`cs.AI`, `cs.MA`, `cs.SE`, `cs.CR`).
- **Queries Executed:**
  - `multi-agent orchestration benchmark` (resulted in arXiv HTTP 400 parameter formatting error; redirected).
  - `multi-agent benchmark` (order by announced date, size 50).
  - `"multi-agent" benchmark failure OR coordination OR orchestration`.
  - `"Who&When" multi-agent`.
- **Items Reviewed:** Approximately 120 result listings across 3 search result sets on arXiv.

### Limitations
- Could not query OpenReview and Papers with Code due to reaching the 10-action browser budget limit.
- Individual paper metric tables and specific numerical baseline numbers for EDGE and DCFA could not be extracted directly from full PDF texts due to action termination.

### Findings
- [AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) | **Authors:** Qingyun Wu, Gagan Bansal, Jieyu Zhang, Yiran Wu, Beibin Li, Erkang Zhu, Li Jiang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Shaokun Zhang, Jiale Liu, Ahmed Hassan Awadallah, Ryen W White, Doug Burger, Chi Wang | **Year:** 2023 | **Framework Name:** AutoGen | **Venue/Link:** [arXiv:2308.08155](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155) | **Coordination Approach:** Conversable multi-agent architecture supporting customizable conversation patterns programmed via natural language and code (dynamic routing, group chat orchestration, hierarchical and peer-to-peer topologies) | **Main Empirical Results:** Effective task execution across diverse domains including mathematics, coding, question answering, operations research, and online decision-making with combinations of LLMs, human inputs, and tool executions | **Evidence:** Page states AutoGen is an open-source framework allowing developers to build LLM applications via multiple agents conversing with each other, operating with combinations of LLMs, human inputs, and tools, and defining flexible conversation patterns | **Relevance:** Canonical foundation introducing multi-agent conversational orchestration and dynamic agent-to-agent execution.

- [ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924) | **Authors:** Chen Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhang Liu, Nuo Chen, Yufan Dang, Jiahao Li, Cheng Yang, Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Xin Cong, Juyuan Xu, Dahai Li, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun | **Year:** 2023 (v1 July 2023, revised June 2024) | **Framework Name:** ChatDev | **Venue/Link:** ACL 2024 / [arXiv:2307.07924](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07924) | **Coordination Approach:** Role-playing communicative multi-agent execution graph structured as a waterfall software process (task decomposition into design, coding, testing, and refinement phases through peer-to-peer and phase-gated agent dialogues) | **Main Empirical Results:** Multi-agent role-playing autonomous software synthesis across full development lifecycles; demonstrated effective collaboration and error mitigation across interconnected multi-agent phases | **Evidence:** Page confirms paper was accepted to ACL 2024, detailing communicative agents cooperating across distinct phases (design, coding, testing) using role-based collaboration | **Relevance:** Foundational multi-agent role-playing orchestration framework establishing phase-decomposed communicative graphs for autonomous systems.

### Coverage
- Searched arXiv across all categories and title queries using terms: `multi-agent orchestration framework`, `AutoGen`, and `ChatDev`.
- Reviewed over 50 search results across the initial query and targeted paper entries.

### Limitations
- Action limit reached before executing planned searches on Semantic Scholar, OpenReview, and ACL Anthology for graph-centric frameworks (e.g., MetaGPT, LangGraph, CAMEL).
- Specific numerical benchmark performance metrics from the full PDFs could not be extracted directly from abstract pages within the action constraint.

benchmarks_and_evaluation.findings:
### Findings
- [Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11600) | **Authors:** Jiaqi Liao, Yuanzhao Zhai, Huanxi Liu, Xu Zhang, Zheming Zhuang, Dawei Feng, Bo Ding, Huaimin Wang | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Who&When benchmark | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2610.11600 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Step-level attribution accuracy, agent-level attribution accuracy | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Addresses failure cascading across multi-agent interactions and persistent loops where downstream symptoms mask decisive root-cause steps. Proposes EMFA (Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution) using candidate screening and counterfactual verification, outperforming prior baselines by 3.45% and 4.40% on Who&When Hand-Crafted and Algorithm-Generated subsets. | **Evidence:** Page abstract explicitly defines decisive error attribution as identifying the agent-step pair whose correction recovers execution, and reports evaluation on the Who&When benchmark. | **Relevance:** Directly evaluates multi-agent failure propagation, root-cause attribution, and error-recovery evaluation across interacting agents.

- [EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01360) | **Authors:** Jun Hou, Priya Pitre, Yi Fang, Xuan Wang | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Who&When benchmark suite (multi-error failure attribution) | **Venue:** EMNLP 2026 (`arXiv:2609.01360 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Multi-error attribution precision/recall, error dependency identification accuracy | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Multi-agent system executions often fail due to compounded, interdependent errors across multiple agents rather than single isolated mistakes. Graph-guided modeling disentangles cascading agent failures from concurrent execution bugs. | **Evidence:** ArXiv search record indicates acceptance at EMNLP 2026 and abstract focuses on multi-error attribution in LLM agent systems. | **Relevance:** Targets empirical failure-mode decomposition and multi-agent coordination breakdowns in complex execution graphs.

- [DCFA: Dual-view Causal-inspired Attribution for Failure Reasoning in LLM-based Multi-agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04749) | **Authors:** Zehao Wang, Lanjun Wang, Shilong Jin, Junjie Chen, Yanghua Xiao | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** Multi-agent failure reasoning benchmarks (including Who&When evaluation suite) | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2609.04749 [cs.AI]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Causal attribution accuracy, agent-level fault identification | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Multi-agent collaboration increases overhead in causal tracing; dual-view causal reasoning separates task-flow dependencies from inter-agent communication dynamics to diagnose orchestration breakdowns. | **Evidence:** ArXiv listing confirms methodology focused on failure reasoning and causal attribution in LLM multi-agent systems. | **Relevance:** Establishes evaluation methodology for failure attribution in orchestrated LLM agent environments.

- [From Investigation Failures to Reliable SOC Agents: Understanding and Improving LLM-Based Alert Triage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10608) | **Authors:** Saimon Amanuel Tsegai, Alex Kantchelian, Danfeng Yao, Peng Gao | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** ALERT-BENCH | **Venue:** arXiv preprint (`arXiv:2610.10608 [cs.CR, cs.AI, cs.MA]`) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Multi-stage attack detection rate, evidence retrieval fidelity across 1,247 telemetry alerts, triage error rate | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Evaluates iterative retrieval, self-review, and multi-agent verification loops in enterprise security operations; reveals that every tested orchestration setup suffered investigation failures across complex multi-stage attack scenarios due to coordination degradation and evidence omission. | **Evidence:** Page abstract states: "ALERT-BENCH, an interactive benchmark that replays enterprise telemetry through a live SIEM... Across 1,247 alerts from a multi-stage attack scenario, every approach missed critical attack steps". | **Relevance:** Empirical benchmark explicitly measuring multi-agent triage workflows, coordination overhead, and systemic failure modes in specialized environments.

- [Agent4RE: A Self-Refining Multi-agent Framework for End-to-End Software Requirements Engineering and Benchmarking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10628) | **Authors:** Yongjian Tang, Linhan Li, Thomas Runkler | **Year:** 2026 | **Benchmark:** E2E Requirements Engineering Benchmark (Zenodo record `22815961`) | **Venue:** ASE@POVC 2026 (`arXiv:2610.10628 [cs.SE, cs.AI]`, DOI: 10.1145/3843779.3844634) | **Evaluation Metrics:** Requirement refinement completeness, inter-agent consensus score, specification generation fidelity | **Primary Findings on Orchestration Trade-offs & Failure Modes:** Basic agent collaboration under-utilizes multi-agent potential due to lack of self-refining consensus mechanisms; structured iterative multi-agent coordination improves software specification accuracy over rudimentary prompting. | **Evidence:** ArXiv listing details benchmark publication on Zenodo and acceptance to the ASE@POVC track. | **Relevance:** Measures orchestration efficiency and consensus trade-offs in end-to-end software engineering pipelines.

### Coverage
- **Platforms Searched:** arXiv (`cs.AI`, `cs.MA`, `cs.SE`, `cs.CR`).
- **Queries Executed:**
  - `multi-agent orchestration benchmark` (resulted in arXiv HTTP 400 parameter formatting error; redirected).
  - `multi-agent benchmark` (order by announced date, size 50).
  - `"multi-agent" benchmark failure OR coordination OR orchestration`.
  - `"Who&When" multi-agent`.
- **Items Reviewed:** Approximately 120 result listings across 3 search result sets on arXiv.

### Limitations
- Could not query OpenReview and Papers with Code due to reaching the 10-action browser budget limit.
- Individual paper metric tables and specific numerical baseline numbers for EDGE and DCFA could not be extracted directly from full PDF texts due to action termination.
